A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dense-SfM by the same authors. Their complete main texts, supplementary material, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original triangulation, camera-pose estimation, ablation, runtime, and novel-view synthesis results in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds comparisons involving MASt3R-SfM, additional VGGSfM pose results, and matching-runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The dense matching, mutual verification, Gaussian Splatting track extension, kernelized refinement, loss, and bundle-adjustment procedures remain unchanged. The IMC quantization workaround already appears in v1. Applying the existing refinement module to MASt3R-SfM and disclosing coarse matching resolutions do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MegaDepth for training and ETH3D, Texture-Poor SfM, IMC 2021, and LLFF for evaluation. IMC moves from v1's supplement into v2's main text. The omitted qualitative cathedral example does not establish removal of that scene from quantitative evaluation.

E2.justification: V2 adds MASt3R-SfM, with and without the proposed refinement, to triangulation and all three pose-estimation comparisons in Tables 1–2. It also adds VGGSfM to the ETH3D and Texture-Poor pose comparisons; v1 already included it for triangulation and IMC. These additions substantially broaden comparisons against alternative SfM pipelines.

E3.justification: The refinement-runtime comparison changes its stated GPU from RTX 4090 in v1 Section 12 to A6000 in v2 Section 7.5. V2 also introduces matching-speed measurements with specified resolutions and A6000 hardware. Existing reconstruction protocols remain; newly disclosed coarse matching resolutions do not establish that earlier accuracy experiments used different settings.

E4.justification: The added MASt3R-SfM comparisons test whether the existing refinement benefits another pipeline, including its accuracy/completeness tradeoff. V2 also adds matching-cost analysis and omits one qualitative cathedral example. The existing component, iteration, track-length, sparse-matching, and semi-dense analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging across scenes remains unchanged. The retained learned correspondence-confidence scores are method outputs, not new statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add substantive MASt3R-SfM refinement and baseline results, plus VGGSfM pose results on ETH3D and Texture-Poor SfM. RoMa + Ours Texture-Poor AUC at 3/5/10 degrees changes from 43.37/60.68/77.87 to 49.94/66.23/81.41 without an explained cause. Refinement timings change from 37.1/44.2 seconds to 35.3/43.2 seconds for DFSfM/Ours on different GPUs; new matching timings are also reported. These timings do not establish a same-setting speed improvement.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, the track definition, Gaussian-process formulation, confidence-weighted loss, and bundle-adjustment objective remain mathematically unchanged. V2's explanation of taking the highest visibility score restates the maximum already present in Equation 3.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the categorical assertion that reconstruction proceeds 'without relying on quantized matching,' modestly narrowing its description. The principal contributions and conclusion remain unchanged. Adding IMC to the introductory evaluation summary reflects results already present in v1's supplement.

C2.justification: V2 Section 7.3 adds an explanation that RoMa's global matching dominates runtime and that lower-resolution coarse matching improves efficiency. The limitations concerning photometric variation and transient occlusions, and the resulting IMC quantization workaround, are already documented in v1 and remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link and documents exhaustive image pairing, coarse RoMa resolutions of 560 × 560 or 420 × 420, subsequent refinement to target resolution, and matching-runtime hardware. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that the underlying implementation changed. Existing Gaussian training schedules and refinement hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: The SfM related-work subsection replaces its classical-pipeline and older learned-BA discussion with differentiable approaches including DUSt3R, MASt3R, MASt3R-SfM, and FlowMap. Several citations are added or removed accordingly, and Global Structure-from-Motion Revisited is added. This updates one literature strand while retaining the central positioning against quantized DFSfM.

P1.justification: V2 clarifies terminology, names previously citation-only methods, rewrites part of related work, and adds acknowledgements. IMC moves into the main experimental narrative, supplementary experiments are regrouped, and references precede the supplement. The main section sequence and most methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 merges v1's main and supplementary pose tables into a three-dataset Table 2 and adds comparison blocks to Tables 1–2. Figures 6–7 become one redesigned Figure 6, retaining six of seven examples. Figures 1–5 retain identical image content, although Figure 5 moves; supplementary tables are reordered and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the paper through broader baseline comparisons, a useful test of refinement on MASt3R-SfM, and additional implementation and runtime documentation. Integrating the existing IMC evaluation also makes the evidence easier to assess. These gains are limited by the unexplained Texture-Poor score revision and insufficient basis for interpreting changed timings as speed improvements; the core method and most supporting experiments remain unchanged.
